Making All Cars Driverless Would Reduce Emissions By 90 Percent

If a fleet of autonomous electric taxis were to replace everyone’s gas-powered, personal cars

I think the keyword here is "electric" not "driveless".

Headline is disingenuous, though. This would take away everyone's private cars and replace them with a fleet of "scheduled" cars that are essentially taxis. The key is that, according to the article, "A fleet about 15 percent of the size of all private cars could service the same population, if scheduled correctly".

So, basically, if you are willing to replace your autonomy with an Uber-like service that "dispatches" cars to you, with the attendant wait times etc, then sure, this kind of thing might be possible. But it won't really be the same thing as simply owning your own vehicle and being able to go where you want, when you want.

So, basically, if you are willing to replace your autonomy with an Uber-like service that "dispatches" cars to you, with the attendant wait times etc,

My digital assistant in my phone (and after July 29th, in every device I own) knows my schedule and lets me know if I need to leave early because of traffic or what not. What's to say it couldn't know my schedule and summon my vehicle anticipating my need for it?

Also, what's to say that driverless cars wouldn't stage themselves based on anticipated need? When you summon your car it wouldn't have to drive to you from downtown or whatever - it might be waiting just around the corner - or one "going your way" might ask it's passenger if they wish to split the cost of a ride with you.

Such a service exists for me today - Car2Go cars are staged in my neighborhood. I can walk less than half a mile, hop in one, and go.

If they were driverless, they could pick me up in probably under 2 minutes.

Car2Go is insanely expensive compared to using your own car, so it's no wonder you have plenty available. It's not a realistic model for a universal service.

As far as the PDA thing, like I said that's the tradeoff. You live according to a predictable schedule, so this kind of thing appeals to you. A lot of people don't.

Remember, I am not saying this kind of thing can't ever work, but I think it's a giant stretch to think it can be done in a way that works for a majority of people, in terms of cost, accessibility, and lifestyle.
